topic: In which US state was basketball invented? (Massachusetts — Springfield, 1891)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

springfield_college.title: The Birthplace of Basketball
springfield_college.notes: invented by instructor/graduate student James Naismith in 1891 at the school (then the International YMCA Training School); janitor brought two peach baskets; nailed to the lower rail of the gym balcony, one at each end — 'the height of that lower balcony rail happened to be ten feet'

wiki_history_basketball.title: History of basketball
wiki_history_basketball.notes: created by Dr James Naismith in December 1891 in Springfield, Massachusetts; peach baskets and a soccer-style ball; 13 rules; class of 18 split into two teams of nine; first public game 11 March 1892

claims.text: Basketball was invented in Springfield, Massachusetts, in December 1891 by James Naismith, an instructor at the International YMCA Training School (now Springfield College).
vo: in which us state was basketball invented
springfield, december eighteen ninety-one, by james naismith

claims.text: Naismith nailed two peach baskets to the lower rail of the gym balcony, one at each end; that rail happened to be ten feet high.
vo: he nailed two peach baskets to a gym balcony rail, exactly ten feet up
screen: Nailed to a balcony rail, 10 ft up.

claims.text: The first game used 13 rules, two teams of nine (a class of 18) and a soccer ball.
vo: thirteen rules, nine a side, and a soccer ball

claims.text: Rims are still 10 feet (3.05 m) above the floor — the height of that 1891 balcony rail.
vo: today's rim is still ten feet

myths.myth: Basketball was invented in Indiana (or by the NBA / in New York).
myths.reality: Indiana's 'Hoosier hysteria' came later; the game began at a Springfield, Massachusetts YMCA school in 1891.

myths.myth: The 10-foot rim was chosen by design.
myths.reality: It was simply the height of the balcony rail the baskets were nailed to.
